articles.title: ​​How Tariffs Are Shaking the Stock Market | Socialnomics
articles.summary: The US stock market has seen its biggest drop in years due to President Trump's announcement of tariffs. Tariffs are a tax levied on imports or exports to boost domestic manufacturing and spending, and to influence world policy and relations with other countries. The US has imposed tariffs on Mexico, Canada, and China, with rates as high as 145% on some Chinese goods. China has retaliated with 125% tariffs on US goods. The technology industry is being hit hard, with companies like Nvidia, Apple, and Dell facing increased costs and limited choices. This could lead to higher prices and reduced economic strain for families. The tariffs have caused uncertainty, leading to changes in stock prices and investors selling stock, causing the DOW to drop 2200 points. However, recent signs of stabilization suggest a cautiously optimistic path forwards for both investors and consumers alike.

articles.title: Key Earnings and Economic Data to Watch This Week: TSLA, GOOGL,
articles.summary: This week, major companies such as Tesla, Alphabet, Intel, and Texas Instruments will release their earnings reports, providing insights into AI demand, cloud services capital expenditure, and tariff impacts. Boeing will also disclose its financials amid concerns about its aircraft orders in China. Additionally, key economic indicators will be released, including the U.S., Eurozone, and UK preliminary Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) data for April. Analysts are particularly focused on the U.S. manufacturing input prices index, which may reflect tariff impacts on costs. The Federal Reserve's Beige Book will also be published, providing a detailed regional economic survey. Fed Chair Jerome Powell recently highlighted potential inflation risks from tariff policies, which may complicate the Fed's policy objectives. Meanwhile, recent remarks from President Trump about Powell have raised concerns about the Fed's independence amid political pressures.

articles.title: Tesla Q1 Earnings Highlights: Revenue Miss, EPS Miss, 'Tariff Landscape' And 'Changing Political Sentiment' Cloud Guidance - Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA)
articles.summary: Tesla reported first-quarter revenue of $19.34 billion, down 9% year-over-year, and earnings of 27 cents per share, down 40% year-over-year. The company delivered 336,681 vehicles, down from 386,810 in the same quarter last year. Tesla's guidance said it is hard to make predictions on the rate of growth for the year due to 'variety of factors' including autonomy efforts, factory production ramp and the macroeconomic environment. The company said it is taking actions to stabilize its Energy business in the medium to long-term and focus on maintaining its health. Tesla also said its plans for more affordable models remain on track to start production in the first half of 2025 and its Robotaxi product, known as the Cybercab, will begin volume production starting in 2026. 'While the current tariff landscape will have a relatively larger impact on our Energy business compared to automotive, we are taking actions to stabilize the business in the medium to long-term and focus on maintaining its health,' the company said. 'We remain committed to expanding our business model to include delivering autonomous robots across multiple form factors and use cases - powered by our real-world AI expertise - to our customers and for use in our factories, as we navigate these headwinds.'

articles.title: Tesla Shareholders Demand Answers On Self-Driving, Cybercab, Tariffs, Brand Damage And More: Their Top 10 Questions Ranked - Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA)
articles.summary: Tesla shareholders have submitted over 6,000 questions for the company's first-quarter earnings call on April 22. The top 10 questions, ranked by the number of shares, include inquiries about full self-driving capabilities, affordable models, tariffs, brand damage, and the Optimus pilot line. Shareholders are concerned about the impact of tariffs on the company's scalability and the recent suspension of plans to ship parts from China for the Cybercab and Tesla Semi. The questions also touch on the company's ability to adapt to global economic risks and the potential for brand damage due to Elon Musk's political push. Analysts expect Tesla to report first-quarter revenue of $21.5 billion and earnings per share of 42 cents, but the company has a history of missing analyst estimates.
